name: Powkiddy V90S

pad.note: oakMOSS's adc-joypad driver (DT adc_gamepad), found by name (POWKIDDY_PAD_NAME, set in V90S.cfg). Confirmed resolving to /dev/input/event1 on the lab unit ; all face/d-pad/shoulder/SELECT/START/MENU codes hardware-verified in the 2026-10-30 guided button test.

lradc.note: the volume keys, on their own LRADC device per PowkiddyCommon.sh's oakmoss_resolve_event_paths; VOL+/VOL- hardware-verified in the same test

power.note: resolved to /dev/input/event2 on the lab unit; the 2026-10-30 button test's capture list includes this node but the test does not press POWER itself

absent.L3: explicit cfg B_L3="DOESNT_EXIST" (V90S.cfg, after sourcing PowkiddyCommon.cfg); no sticks on this board. The 2026-10-30 hardware test's header states 'no sticks, no L3/R3'
absent.FN_SWITCH: no switch; device_get_switch_position is the oakMOSS no-op stub (PowkiddyCommon.sh does not override it)
absent.LID: clamshell hinge, but spruce does not read a lid on this board: the stock DT carries a disabled MH248 hall node ('hall_para', interrupt PL9) that is unverified as wired, and oakMOSS's device_lid_open (oakMOSSCommon.sh) always returns '1' regardless. Knulli's capability list names 'lid' for the V90S, but no public source shows how lid-close is detected there either.

notes: The strongest-evidenced manifest of the six: a 2026-10-30 guided button test on the lab unit (.82, B233) hardware-verified every control this manifest lists as present, and its header independently confirms no sticks and no L3/R3.
POWER itself was not pressed in that test (its capture list only shows the node was recorded); treat the code as cfg-only until a run presses it.

The V90S lid and FF rumble remain the biggest open items per the 2026-10-23 research (needs a unit that shows the hall sensor wired); rumble is out of scope for this manifest (not a Button Reader control).
